rounds.text: NGL Fine Chem Ltd is demonstrating extraordinary fundamental momentum, led by compounded sales growth of 36% over the trailing twelve months and a staggering 130% compounded profit growth over the same period [E17, E21]. Operational efficiency is expanding rapidly, highlighted by an operating margin of 12% in March 2026 compared to just 4% in the year-ago quarter [E31]. This explosive growth is underpinned by heavy reinvestment, with Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) surging 90.0% to Rs 95 Cr, signaling major growth spend underway for future capacity [E40]. Institutional participation is reflecting this operational strength with positive money flow, and the healthcare sector provides a strong macro tailwind with a tailwind score above one [E44, E72]. Market participants are validating this trajectory through immense relative strength, driving the stock to its 52-week high with a 156.5% twelve-month price return while trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E49, E50, E52]. conceded: [E45], [E46], [E69]

NGL Fine Chem Ltd trades at an extreme valuation premium, evidenced by a trailing P/E of 48.7x [E1] and a sector-beating EV/EBITDA of 23.91x against the sector benchmark of 20.84x [E11]. Fundamental value models sound a clear alarm, with a discounted cash flow estimating intrinsic value at Rs 752 per share against a market price of Rs 3,280, resulting in a severe margin of safety deficit of -336.3% [E45, E46]. This detachment from underlying reality is further highlighted by a reverse DCF implying that today's price demands 20.4% earnings growth, even though the base case assumes 0.0% [E47]. Compounding the valuation risk, the company exhibits negative long-term profit performance with a 5-year compounded profit growth of -6% [E19] and a low 3-year median return on equity of 12% [E28]. Capital intensity is also rising sharply, with borrowings climbing to Rs 108 Cr [E39], negative free cash flow reaching -51 Cr [E36], and capital-work-in-progress surging by 90.0% to Rs 95 Cr [E40]. conceded: [E50]

The bear's valuation alarm via the DCF of Rs 752 [E45] ignores that the company's rules-based screen scores a solid 79 out of 100 with a BUY rating [E62]. While the bear cites 5-year profit contraction [E19], it completely overlooks explosive recent momentum, including a 130% surge in trailing twelve-month profit growth [E21], a 36% jump in trailing sales [E17], and management being expected to deliver a good upcoming quarter [E59]. The concern over rising borrowings to Rs 108 Cr [E39] and negative free cash flow [E36] is the natural consequence of a massive 90% expansion in capital-work-in-progress to Rs 95 Cr [E40], representing active growth spend underway rather than structural distress. Furthermore, the healthcare sector itself is firmly in a strong tailwind with a score of +1.06 [E72], perfectly supporting the company's accelerating top-line performance. Conceded: [E1, E11, E28, E47].

Conceded: [E62], [E59]. The bull's reliance on a rules-based score of 79/100 [E62] ignores that the same engine explicitly flags the DCF as overvalued by 336% [E68] and warns that earnings growth is decelerating [E67]. While explosive trailing twelve-month profit growth of 130% [E21] and 36% sales growth [E17] sound impressive, they mask a multi-year trend where 5-year profit growth sits at -6% [E19] and 5-year share price growth is completely flat at 0% [E23], proving that long-term fundamental delivery has historically lagged behind price action [E56]. Dismissing the negative free cash flow of -51 Cr [E36] and rising borrowings of 108 Cr [E39] as merely a consequence of a 90% surge in CWIP [E40] ignores the reality that capital expenditure has currently destroyed free cash generation and inflated debt liabilities. Furthermore, sector tailwinds [E72] do not insulate a stock trading at an elevated P/E of 48.7x [E1] and a Price-to-Book ratio of 6.33x [E2] that commands a massive -336.3% margin of safety against intrinsic value [E46].
